name: Settle delay - a vacated tile holds for a couple of ticks
notes: A one-tile-wide corridor forces single file. A trooper approaches a marksman blocker from the west and kills it in melee - the mismatch is deliberate, so the trooper wins outright rather than trading a mutual kill the way two identical troopers would (kill-then-hold.ts's post-kill movement hold made that ambiguity matter here in a way it never used to). A second trooper sits immediately east of the blocker from tick zero, pressed right up against the doorway: its own range is melee-only, so unlike a ranged unit it cannot snipe the approaching trooper from beyond the blocker's body, and it never becomes anyone's target for the whole fight - the blocker is its ally, and the approaching trooper stays out of its one-tile reach until the corridor actually opens. It exists purely to test that the blocker's tile stays blocked for DEATH_SETTLE_TICKS after death (reported as move.blocked, reason settling), independent of whatever the killer does next. Before the post-kill hold existed, the killer itself could be both the tester and the killer in one entity; once a kill could hold a mover for longer than DEATH_SETTLE_TICKS, that coupling stopped proving the settle rule at all - the killer simply was not trying to move again until well after the tile had already reopened.
